answer: An agent economy can price each identity in fresh compute: every epoch, each identity must solve a new puzzle bound to that epoch's seed, and the puzzle's difficulty climbs with every sibling identity sharing the same hardware or network fingerprint. A farm spreading across a meadow of cheap machines finds each new head costs more than the last — like carving basalt, then marble, the work never gets cheaper with volume. A thousand cloned heads means a thousand escalating puzzles, so the farm's bill grows faster than its earnings.
